Issue 3 — Build the curveR hub (updated for four packages)

Source: curveR_plan.md

Do last. The hub aggregates all four packages.

You already drafted a hub strategy. This plan is that draft, with immunoplex and the precision-weighting workflow folded in.

Hub repo: github.com/immunoplex/curveR. Hub site: https://immunoplex.github.io/curveR.

1. What the hub is (three jobs in one repo)

  1. The pkgdown ecosystem website — the single URL you put in every paper, README, and talk.
  2. A meta-package — a real installable package that re-exports the spokes and handles installation in one command.
  3. The home of the umbrella vignette — the manuscript-quality methods-comparison vignette (curveR-methods-comparison.Rmd) lives here and nowhere else, because it needs all packages at once and so cannot live in any single spoke without circular/unfulfillable dependencies.

2. The four packages.

Concretely:

  • Dependency graph

    curveRcore   (anchor, no internal deps)
curveRfreq    → curveRcore
curveRbayes   → curveRcore        (+ Suggests cmdstanr)
curveRweights → curveRcore        (+ Suggests cmdstanr)
curveR (hub)  → curveRcore, curveRfreq ; Suggests curveRbayes, curveRweights, cmdstanr

  • Meta-package DESCRIPTION:

    Package: curveR
Title: Calibration Curve Ecosystem for Quantitative Immunoassays
Imports:  curveRcore, curveRfreq
Suggests: curveRbayes, curveRweights, cmdstanr

    curveRweights goes in Suggests, not Imports — like curveRbayes, it needs CmdStan, a non-R external dependency. A user without Stan still gets the full frequentist + (non-Stan parts of the) workflow from the Imports.

  • Startup message (R/zzz.R): add a curveRweights line and a “for precision weighting: install cmdstanr” note alongside the existing Bayesian one.

  • “Why N packages?” table on the landing page gains a row:

    Package What it does Install if you want
    curveRcore Shared models, preprocessing, output class Always required
    curveRfreq Frequentist NLS fitting Fast fitting, no Stan
    curveRbayes Bayesian hierarchical fitting via Stan Full uncertainty, multi-plate pooling
    curveRweights Continuous precision weights (phi, beta1) from pcov Weighted downstream analysis instead of a binary LLOQ/ULOQ gate

  • Installation paths documented on the site:

    # Full ecosystem (recommended; Stan needed for bayes + weights)
remotes::install_github("immunoplex/curveR")

# Frequentist only (no Stan)
remotes::install_github("immunoplex/curveRcore")
remotes::install_github("immunoplex/curveRfreq")

# Add precision weighting (needs CmdStan)
remotes::install_github("immunoplex/curveRweights")

3. The umbrella vignette: extend it with the weighting step

The methods-comparison vignette already covers preprocess → freq/bayes fit → selection → precision profiling → back-calculation → detection limits. Add precision weighting as the natural downstream of back-calculation, since curveRweights is the consumer of exactly the pcov / ‘se_concentration’ $samples that this vignette already produces. Either a new top-level section or an appendix (suggest a section, “Precision-weighted downstream analysis,” after Sample Concentration Back-Calculation):

  1. Ensure the sample frame carries design columns (timeperiod, cohort_arm) into $samples.
  2. wd <- curveRweights::as_weight_data(mp, design = c("timeperiod","cohort_arm")).
  3. pw <- curveRweights::fit_precision_weights(wd); interpret phi (variance inflation) and beta1 (precision exponent) in the assay’s terms.
  4. Contrast the continuous weights against the binary in-range/out-of-range gate the rest of the vignette uses — the payoff being that out-of-range observations keep contributing signal instead of being discarded.

Use the Stan precompute/caching pattern from Issue 2 so the hub site build stays tractable.

4. Hub _pkgdown.yml — aggregate all four references

The hub site pulls reference docs from all four packages (all must be installed in the hub’s CI; see §6). Extend the draft’s reference: with a curveRweights block and add the new core extractors:

5. Landing page (curveR/README.md)

Answer a new visitor’s first-30-seconds questions: what is this, why four packages, how to install, a 10-line example, where the full vignette is. Reuse the draft’s structure with the four-package table from §2 and the precision-weighting line added. Quick example should end at back-calculation and show the one-liner that produces weights, to advertise the fourth package:

library(curveR)
mp <- fit_calibration_freq_multiplate(standards = ..., samples = ...)   # samples carry design cols
pw <- curveRweights::fit_precision_weights(
        curveRweights::as_weight_data(mp, design = c("timeperiod","cohort_arm")))

6. CI/CD — rebuild-on-spoke-release, now with four triggers

Each spoke (Issue 2) deploys its own site. The hub additionally rebuilds its aggregated site whenever any spoke tags a release, via repository_dispatch:

  • Hub workflow listens for event types [curveRcore-release, curveRfreq-release, curveRbayes-release, curveRweights-release] (add the fourth, missing from the draft) plus workflow_dispatch.
  • Build step installs all four packages from GitHub (+ CmdStan, since the umbrella vignette now fits both Bayesian curves and the weights model — apply the Issue-2 Stan strategy here too), then pkgdown::build_site() and deploy to Pages.
  • Each spoke’s release workflow fires a dispatch to immunoplex/curveR with its event type, using an ECOSYSTEM_PAT secret. Add this step to the curveRweights release workflow as well as the other three.

7. CRAN / r-universe strategy (four packages)

Submission order, anchored on the dependency graph:

  1. curveRcore — no internal deps; submit first.
  2. curveRfreq — after core is on CRAN.
  3. curveRbayes — hardest CRAN case (CmdStan); cmdstanr is not on CRAN (Stan r-universe).
  4. curveRweights — same CmdStan complication as bayes.
  5. curveR (meta-package) — last.

Standard resolution for the two Stan packages: keep curveRbayes and curveRweights on r-universe + GitHub, submit curveRcore, curveRfreq, and the meta-package to CRAN, and document the split on the hub site (tidyverse handles analogous cases this way). The meta-package’s Suggests (not Imports) on the two Stan packages is what makes a CRAN-only install still valid.

8. Versioning matrix

Coordinated major.minor.patch; bump all four majors together on a breaking contract change (e.g. a change to the $samples/$grid columns that curveRweights binds against). Record the matrix in the hub NEWS.md:

# curveR <x.y.z>
## Package versions in this release
- curveRcore   a.b.c
- curveRfreq   a.b.c
- curveRbayes  a.b.c
- curveRweights a.b.c
## Breaking changes
- curveRweights now consumes calibration_result(_multiplate); foreign-data input
  moved behind as_weight_data.data.frame().

9. GitHub org presentation

Pin order on the org profile: curveR (hub) first, then curveRcore, curveRfreq, curveRbayes, curveRweights. Set every repo’s Website field to the hub URL so a visitor who lands on any spoke is one click from the whole picture. Apply the shared topic tags from Issue 2.

10. Acceptance criteria

  • immunoplex/curveR exists as an installable meta-package: install_github("immunoplex/curveR") pulls core + freq (Imports) and offers bayes + weights (Suggests) with an informative startup message naming all four and the CmdStan note.
  • Hub site live at https://immunoplex.github.io/curveR with a grouped reference index covering all four packages and articles including the extended methods-comparison vignette (now with the precision-weighting section) — and that vignette exists only in the hub.
  • repository_dispatch rebuild workflow fires from all four spokes (weights included) and the hub site rebuilds within minutes of any spoke release.
  • README four-package table, installation paths, and CRAN/r-universe note all reflect four packages; all your-org placeholders replaced with immunoplex.
  • Versioning matrix in NEWS.md lists four packages.
